title: How Zero Was Invented: The Story of Nothing
meta_description: Discover how zero developed from a placeholder into a number, why Indian mathematicians transformed arithmetic, and how the idea spread around the world.
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: Zero has two distinct roles: it can mark an empty place in a positional numeral system, and it can be treated as a number in calculations.
The history of zero was gradual rather than a single invention. Several ancient cultures used placeholders, but a fully developed arithmetic treatment emerged in India.
Brahmagupta's 628 CE mathematical work gave rules for calculations involving zero and negative numbers, although some rules involving division by zero were not correct by modern standards.
The Bakhshali manuscript contains a dot used as a placeholder, but dating its layers is complex and it should not simply be described as the first modern zero.
